paragraphs: Children in care in Leeds are looked after by Foster4Leeds, Leeds City Council's own fostering service, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. The council says more than 1,500 children are in its care, and that when it cannot find a suitable Foster4Leeds carer it has to turn to residential care or an independent agency, which can mean a placement outside the city. Foster4Leeds describes itself as a not-for-profit service and says that local carers help children stay at the same school and keep in touch with family and friends.

In its recruitment appeals the council has said it is especially short of carers for young people aged 11 and over, for brothers and sisters who need to live together, and for children with disabilities or additional needs.

Foster4Leeds pays carers a weekly allowance for each child and a weekly fee linked to the carer's skills; it publishes its current rates on its own website rather than in its news releases, so ask the service for the figures that apply now. It also points to training, free counselling, days out and short breaks for fostering families. For council staff who foster, it offers paid leave for assessment, training and panel, and the right to ask for flexible working.

Every service sets its own pay and support, so it is worth speaking to Foster4Leeds and two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you decide.
